subject: Re: Renewal — premium SLA + support tier for FinTechX
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Anna Kaplan <anna.kaplan@fintechx.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 25 Feb 2026 09:17:00 -0800
Subject: Renewal conversation — premium SLA & support tier

Anna —

Happy Friday. As we approach your March 15 renewal, I wanted to put a concrete proposal on the table to support FinTechX’s growing production needs. Based on the usage profile and the latency sensitivity you shared, we recommend the following changes for the upcoming 12‑month renewal: 

• Upgrade to Premium SLA (SLA-2) with 99.95% uptime and a 99th-percentile latency SLO of 120ms for gen endpoints.
• Move to Premium Support Tier: 24/7 on-call, 15‑minute P1 response, monthly QBRs with a named TAM.
• Capacity increase: reserve an additional dedicated pool of 4× A100-equivalent GPUs with burst to shared for peak payroll windows.

I attached a draft order (RI_PremiumSLA_FinTechX_Q1-2026.pdf) with the delta pricing and a short SLO matrix (latency_slo_matrix.xlsx). Key asks from your side: confirmation that the proposed P99 target meets your requirements and an estimate of expected token volume growth during April–June so we can finalize pricing.

If it helps, Laura can jump on a 30‑minute tech call early next week to walk the team through the latency guarantees and fallbacks.

Thanks — look forward to locking this in so we can schedule the capacity change ahead of payroll season.

— Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai
(415) 555-0192

Attachments: RI_PremiumSLA_FinTechX_Q1-2026.pdf (proposal), latency_slo_matrix.xlsx (SLO/metrics)
From: Anna Kaplan <anna.kaplan@fintechx.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Daniel Cho <daniel.cho@fintechx.com>
Date: Thu, 26 Feb 2026 11:02:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Renewal conversation — premium SLA & support tier

Marissa —

Thanks for the proposal and clear options. A couple quick clarifying questions from our side: 

1) The P99 120ms target — is that measured from request arrival at your public API endpoint or from our VPC egress IP? We need the SLO to reflect our end-to-end latency (tenant edge to token complete) for legal/regulatory reasons.
2) If the SLA is missed twice in a quarter, how are credits applied? We need a clear crediting formula for our procurement team.
3) On capacity, the additional pool sounds right. Can you confirm whether the dedicated pool will be isolated (no noisy-neighbor noisy effects) and whether autoscale will trigger during our batch payroll runs?

We have procurement loops that need the DocuSign + order form; can you send a DocuSign link and a final quote?

Anna Kaplan
Head of Platform Engineering, FinTechX
anna.kaplan@fintechx.com
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Anna Kaplan <anna.kaplan@fintechx.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 27 Feb 2026 08:34:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Renewal conversation — premium SLA & support tier

Anna — thanks, great questions. Quick answers and next steps: 

1) Measurement: the P99 we included is measured at the ingress load balancer in Redwood’s control plane (public API). For end-to-end tenant‑edge measurement we can add an edge probe from your VPC (agent) and include that as an optional telemetry target in the contract. That will require an addendum (we’ve added the text in the attached draft).

2) Credits: standard credit ladder is pro-rated service-days credit for severity and duration. For premium SLA we can add a deterministic formula: for each distinct SLA breach window where P99 > 120ms for > 30 minutes, a 5% monthly credit is applied to that month’s bill; subsequent breaches escalate (8% then 12%). We can make this explicit in Section 4 of the order form.

3) Isolation & autoscale: the dedicated pool will be tenant-isolated (no other customers share the physical GPUs), and autoscale will be configured with a burst policy to the shared cluster capped at 20% additional capacity during peak windows. For payroll windows we recommend pre-warming the pool 48 hours ahead; Aditya can outline the pre-warm steps below.

Next steps: Laura — can you confirm the technical pre-warm runbook and whether any model-variant pinning is required to avoid cold cache miss during the payroll spike? Aditya — can you confirm the timeline to create the dedicated pool and the expected provisioning lead time? I’ll prepare the DocuSign with the agreed credit formula if you confirm the measurement approach.

Best,
Marissa

-----Original Message-----

(Attached: updated draft order with addendum)
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 27 Feb 2026 10:04:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Renewal conversation — premium SLA & support tier (internal)

Marissa / Aditya —

Quick tech notes for the record: 

• Pre-warm runbook: 1) replicate recent traffic profile (token distribution) into a staging namespace; 2) run continuous prefix caching for 48h; 3) verify KV hit rate > 85% and P99 < 100ms on staging; 4) schedule cutover during low-traffic window (we recommend 02:00–06:00 local).
• Model pinning: recommend pinning the production T5-XL variant for the payroll endpoints to avoid transparent reloads during peak — this increases memory but reduces cold-start risk.
• Provisioning lead time: dedicated pool of 4 GPUs -> 5 business days from signed order + confirmed capacity allocation; if they need an earlier date we can provision a temporary burst pool but cost will be higher for the interim week.

I can join Anna’s call next week to walk through the runbook.

— Laura
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Anna Kaplan <anna.kaplan@fintechx.com>, FinTechX Procurement <procurement@fintechx.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 01 Mar 2026 14:22:00 -08:00
Subject: Updated order & DocuSign (SLA credit formula included)

Anna / Procurement —

Thanks for the quick clarifying questions — I’ve attached a finalized order with the SLA credit ladder made explicit and the edge-probe addendum for end-to-end measurement. The DocuSign link below is live and includes: 

• Premium SLA terms (P99 120ms at ingress; optional edge probe addendum to measure e2e latency)
• Exact credit formula for breaches (5% / 8% / 12% per month as discussed)
• Capacity reservation: 4 dedicated GPUs + burst policy to shared pool (20% cap)
• Premium Support: named TAM, 24/7 P1 on-call, monthly QBRs

DocuSign: https://redwood.app/docusign/abc123
Order form attached: FinTechX_order_form_signed_stub.pdf (final pricing summary)

If procurement needs a single consolidated invoice line for the SLA delta let me know — we can issue a one-line charge labeled “Premium SLA & Dedicated Capacity — Mar–Mar 2027”.

Best — I’ll check back mid-week for signatures.

— Marissa
From: Anna Kaplan <anna.kaplan@fintechx.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: FinTechX Procurement <procurement@fintechx.com>, Daniel Cho <daniel.cho@fintechx.com>
Date: Mon, 02 Mar 2026 16:03:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Updated order & DocuSign (SLA credit formula included)

Marissa —

This looks good. Procurement has reviewed the DocuSign and the credit ladder; Daniel is looping our legal on the edge probe addendum. We will sign and return by EOD Wednesday. One final ask from procurement: please include the Master Service Agreement (MSA) revision summary page as a single PDF bound to the DocuSign envelope so our contract team can stamp.

Also, confirming that provisioning lead time is 5 business days after signature — we will target Mar 22 as the go-live (pre-warm scheduled Mar 20).

Thanks to you and the team for moving fast.

— Anna

Attachments referenced: none in this message (DocuSign link active).
